'''Sir Robert Hughes Williams''', {{post-nominals|country=GBR|sep=,|CBE|FRS|FLSW|HonFInstP}} (born 22 December 1941), commonly known as '''Robin Williams''', is a Welsh physicist and academic specialising in [[solid state physics]] and [[semiconductors]], and [[Chancellor of Bangor University]].

==Early life==
Born on a hill farm at [[Llanuwchllyn]], after attending the village school there Williams was educated at [[Ysgol y Berwyn|Bala Grammar School]] before studying Physics at the [[University College of North Wales]], where he graduated [[Bachelor of Science|BSc]] and [[Doctor of philosophy|PhD]].<ref name=BA>[https://www.thebangoraye.com/bangor-university-appoints-new-chancellor/ "BANGOR UNIVERSITY APPOINTS NEW CHANCELLOR"], ''The Bangor Aye'', 29 November 2022</ref>

==Career==
Williams is an authority on [[semiconductors]], and his research work has  furthered [[digital electronics]]. He has developed new methods for the study of semiconductors and was an early user of [[synchrotron radiation]] to study the surfaces of solids.<ref name=BA/>

He taught at the [[New University of Ulster]] and the [[University of Wales, College of Cardiff]], before serving as [[Vice-Chancellor]] of the [[University of Wales, Swansea]], from  1994 to 2003.<ref name="WW 2019">{{cite web |title=Williams, Prof. Robert Hughes, (Robin) |url=https://www.ukwhoswho.com/view/10.1093/ww/9780199540884.001.0001/ww-9780199540884-e-40055 |website=[[Who's Who 2019]] |publisher=Oxford University Press |access-date=8 June 2019 |language=en |doi=10.1093/ww/9780199540884.013.U40055 |date=1 December 2018|isbn=978-0-19-954088-4 }}</ref><ref name="HEFCW">{{cite web |title=Professor Robin Williams CBE, FRS |url=https://www.hefcw.ac.uk/council_and_committees/council_members/professor_robin_williams.aspx |website=Higher Education Funding Council for Wales - hefcw |access-date=8 June 2019 |archive-date=8 June 2019 |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20190608153622/https://www.hefcw.ac.uk/council_and_committees/council_members/professor_robin_williams.aspx |url-status=dead }}</ref><ref name="GOV">{{cite web |title=BIRTHDAY HONOURS 2019 – HIGH AWARDS |url=https://assets.publishing.service.gov.uk/government/uploads/system/uploads/attachment_data/file/807355/Birthday-Honours-2019_-Higher-awards.docx.pdf |website=GOV.UK |access-date=8 June 2019 |date=2019}}</ref>

==Honours==
In 1990, Williams was elected a [[Fellow of the Royal Society]] (FRS), the United Kingdom's national academy for the sciences.<ref name="FRS">{{cite web |title=Professor Robert Williams CBE FRS |url=https://royalsociety.org/people/robert-williams-12527/ |website=Royal Society |access-date=8 June 2019 |language=en-gb}}</ref> In 2010, he was elected a [[Learned Society of Wales|Founding Fellow of the Learned Society of Wales]] (FLSW).<ref name="FLSW">{{cite web |title=Yr Athro Robin Williams CBE HonFInstP FLSW FRS |url=https://www.learnedsociety.wales/fellow/robin-williams/ |website=The Learned Society of Wales |access-date=8 June 2019}}</ref>

He was appointed [[Commander of the Order of the British Empire]] (CBE) in the [[2004 New Year Honours]] for services to education and to the community in Swansea<ref name="LG 57155">{{London Gazette |issue= 57155 |date= 31 December 2003 |pages= 7-9 |supp= y }}</ref> and [[Knight Bachelor|knighted]] in the [[2019 Birthday Honours]] for services to higher education, research and the Welsh language.<ref name="LG 62666">{{London Gazette |issue= 62666 |date= 8 June 2019 |page= B2 |supp= y }}</ref>
